name: Shucks Mordant
designNotes:
EXPANDED 2026-09-21 at Ingram's request, in the same pass as Manako's. This is now a working brief a GM can run him from at any point in the campaign; `quarantine/ideas/story/bible/characters/shucks-mordant.md` remains the source and is where anything contested gets corrected first.

Full history, voice notes and open questions live in quarantine/ideas/story/bible/characters/shucks-mordant.md -- read that in full before writing any scene with him. THIS FILE FORMALIZES HIM AS A REAL ENTITY for the first time (data/npcs/ previously held only the three Directorate poles and six repair-crew-chief placeholders); it adds nothing his bible file doesn't already establish.

Tone, load-bearing: his revenge-list placement is LATER-CAMPAIGN information and must not leak backward into how he plays in Episode One or any early scene (his founder status is not: LEDGER #28 reveals it at the start) -- he reads as untroubled, not as a man with a secret.

Proposed connection, 2026-09-12, NOT YET CONFIRMED BY INGRAM: while grounding data/locations/general-hospital.json (the fortress island's main hospital -- a separate, larger building from the campus's Intake Medicals hall he staffs personally), his title 'Chief Medical Officer' was read as plausibly extending to administrative oversight of the island's whole medical apparatus, hospital included, even though he is never there in person. That is a reasonable extrapolation of an already-settled title, not a new invention, but it directly touches his own bible file's open question 'what has he actually done for two hundred years besides staff intake medicals' without resolving it -- flagged there rather than settled here, and surfaced directly to Ingram for confirmation. If Ingram would rather the hospital answer to nobody in particular, or to someone else entirely, general-hospital.json's npcRefs is a one-line change.

TWO OPEN ARCS LIVE IN THE BIBLE FILE AND NOT HERE, deliberately, because both are unresolved by design: `arc-shucks-hand` (where the hand is, what it knows, whether it ever meets the party) and `arc-what-shucks-said` (what he says behind the Deputy Director's door and why he has the standing to say it -- four live candidates, none decided). Do not settle either in passing.

THE HAND NOW HAS ITS OWN FILE: it is Rand (LEDGER #34), quarantine/ideas/story/bible/characters/rand.md.
status: DRAFT -- expanded 2026-09-21 at Ingram's request into a full working brief.

facts.text: His right hand is a very convincing prosthetic.

revealTrigger.narrative: Passing `the-hand` in `c1e1-the-medical` (Perception or Medicine, DC 17). This Fact is that check's persistent form -- once it lands, it stays known for the rest of the campaign rather than being rediscovered.

facts.text: He is not permitted to say what the blood screen tests for, he thinks the rule is stupid, and he will say that it is stupid. Asking again does not move him and does not annoy him either.

revealTrigger.narrative: Asking him about the screen at all. He refuses warmly and volunteers his opinion of the rule unprompted.

facts.text: He talks about students across a span of years that does not add up, and he does it without noticing. He is not hiding his age; it has simply never occurred to him that it is remarkable.

He has processed intakes for long enough to have taken blood from a candidate's grandparents, and he says so without making anything of it. Pressed on how long, he answers honestly and immediately, and the honesty is more disconcerting than evasion would have been.

revealTrigger.narrative: Asking him how long he has been doing this, which he answers straight.

facts.text: The thing he will not explain is a rule imposed on him, not a confidence he is keeping, and he thinks the rule is stupid. He will not break it and he will not defend it either. Anybody who reads him gets both halves clearly.

revealTrigger.narrative: Pushing him on the screen result and watching what he does with the refusal.

facts.text: If the hand comes up at all, he is completely unbothered. It is off doing its own thing, he does not know where, and it will turn up when it is hungry. He talks about it the way somebody talks about a cat that has taken to staying out.

revealTrigger.narrative: Noticing the prosthetic and asking about it rather than letting it go.
